headline: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: In fiscal year 2026 budget talks, the fire chief said a $15 million Haʻikū Fire Station grant was lost, and planning cited uncompetitive salaries.
meeting.recap: The planning director said the department's salaries are not competitive.[[0:07:14]] The planning director said the department reviews every Lahaina building permit as part of Lahaina recovery.[[0:08:19]] The deputy planning director said the department has 24 vacancies.[[0:09:38]] The fire chief said four changes to the fire budget would save $76,936.[[0:16:33]] The fire chief said the department lost a $15 million federal grant for Haʻikū Fire Station.[[0:16:48]] A firefighter testifier asked that travel costs for firefighters working on Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi be covered, as they are for police.[[0:22:44]] The fire chief said the department already pays for firefighters' flights and ferry tickets to Molokaʻi.[[1:22:05]] Planning said it will work with the Department of Housing to get county-owned land approved for housing.[[2:17:59]] Planning said a $250,000 study of the shoreline special management area boundary will go out for bids.[[2:22:53]] Members were asked to send extra questions to committee staff by 9 o'clock tomorrow.[[3:00:30]] The meeting was adjourned.[[3:01:33]]
meeting.next: Planning said the shoreline boundary study would give recommendations to the Maui Planning Commission.

moments.q: "We are investing in our most valuable resource, our people."
Fire chief explains loss of the $15 million Haʻikū Fire Station grant

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: Planning is asking for consultant money to get county-owned land approved for housing.
issues.next: Housing will help pick a parcel, and planning will work with a consultant on the approvals.
issues.brief: Planning said the effort is a joint project with the Department of Housing, modeled on a County of Kauaʻi project.[[#1]] Planning said work on county-owned land approvals funded last year was not done.[[#2]] The fire chief said $36,000 in new rent money would rent a house for Molokaʻi firefighters instead of buying one.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: The planning department says Lahaina recovery permit reviews add to its heavy workload.
issues.why: The planning director said the department reviews each Lahaina building permit and does a close review of shoreline projects.
issues.brief: A contractor working through Public Works is helping planning review building permits for West Maui.[[#1]] The deputy planning director said some businesses from Lahaina are moving to Kīhei, Wailuku or other areas and filing permits there.[[#2]]
